key_insight: The paper shows that RGB-D segmentation models can be made much more reliable when one modality is missing by continuing training with a simple condition dropout strategy. Instead of failing under sensor loss, the model learns to use whichever modality is still available.
problem_solved: It addresses the real-world problem that RGB-D semantic segmentation models are usually trained assuming both RGB and depth are always present, so performance drops sharply when a sensor fails, is occluded, or is unavailable at test time.
method: Introduces Condition Dropout (ConD), a continued-training paradigm that randomly drops one modality during training.
Forces the model to learn from RGB-only, depth-only, and full RGB-D inputs so it becomes robust to missing modalities.
Retains the benefits of full-modality training while improving adaptability when surveillance or sensing conditions are incomplete.
impact: This makes RGB-D segmentation systems more dependable in practical deployments where sensors are imperfect or unavailable. For practitioners, it offers a simple training-time fix that can improve robustness without requiring major architectural changes.
visual_elements: A side-by-side pipeline showing full RGB-D input versus missing RGB or missing depth at test time

paper_title: Toward Reliable RGB-D Semantic Segmentation: Handling Missing Modalities via Condition Dropout
paper_authors: Xuchen Zhu, Yajuan Wei, Shuang Hao, Jiwei Jiang, Guanxiang Mao
